Ceilings & services

Each room in an office asks something different of its ceiling.

A single ceiling specification across a whole floor is simple to buy and rarely right. Taking the plan room by room reveals what each space needs overhead, and where no ceiling is needed at all.

Sound & concentration

The false ceiling is the largest acoustic surface in an office.

A ceiling can absorb noise within a room or stop it passing between rooms, but rarely both by default. Understanding the difference shapes the choice of material, layout and detail.

Light & atmosphere

Lighting an office begins at the window and ends at the ceiling.

Good office lighting is a sequence of decisions, starting with daylight and the façade, then layering artificial light, controlling glare and letting the ceiling carry it all.
